title: Google will now let any AI agent run your smart home
slides: Google just handed control of your smart home to AI?
Any AI agent can now trigger lights, locks, and cameras.
But Google's own Gemini won't get special access.
Check your permissions: third-party agents can now act freely.
Revoke access for any agent you don't fully trust today.
thread_text:
1. Google Just Gave AI the Keys

Any AI agent can now trigger your lights, locks, and cameras. Google's own Gemini doesn't get special access.

2. The Permission Problem

Third-party agents can act freely without Gemini's restrictions. Google opened the door to every AI developer.

3. Gemini Locked Out

Google's own assistant plays by different rules. Competitors get broader access than the home team.

4. Your Home, Their Playground

Check your permissions today. Unknown agents may already have control over your smart devices.

5. Take Action Now

Revoke access for any agent you don't fully trust. Do it today before something unexpected happens.

instagram.caption:
Your lights, locks, and cameras can now be triggered by AI agents you've never heard of.

Google opened its smart home platform to any AI agent, not just its own.

Third-party developers now get broader access than Gemini, Google's own assistant, which plays by different rules.

If you publish smart home content, your audience's devices may already be exposed to agents they didn't approve.

Open your Google Home app, check connected apps, and revoke anything you don't fully trust. 🔒

Which agent has access to your front door right now? 🚪
